speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I came down for a roll in Garnish's basket. I did not know the parlour was a fitting.

speaker: edith_kettlewood
text: The basket can wait. The doublet cannot. Autumn's work, Master Shakespeare. The sleeve is mended. The account is not.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The seam is finer than the old one. You have made the rent disappear. I would have said so even if you had come only to show it.

speaker: edith_kettlewood
text: I have heard the praise. The praise does not pay the eight shillings. Sit down, if you mean to look, and do not let the looking become the settlement.

speaker: john_heminges
text: The eight shillings is the company's, from the autumn, and it is still owing. I am not going to pretend a compliment has a date on it.

speaker: edith_kettlewood
text: I have made him a prince. The prince still owes eight shillings.

speaker: will_kemp
text: Pay the woman. Then tell me what we cannot afford. A prince who cannot pay for his sleeves should keep his arms inside his coat.

speaker: edith_kettlewood
text: I heard you, Master Kemp. I am not laughing. Write it, one of you, or take the doublet back unmended in your account, which would be a lie, because I have mended it.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: It is not my debt. I will write it anyway, if writing is what you are waiting on. John, say the day.

speaker: john_heminges
text: Lady Day is the latest I can promise. Not before, unless the money comes, and I will not promise the before.

speaker: edith_kettlewood
text: Lady Day. Say it as a day and not as a kindness. I will wait on a day. I will not wait on a speech about the seam.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Then look at the tables, not the seam.

speaker: edith_kettlewood
text: I cannot see it from here. Turn it.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Edith viij s. owing. Lady Day. That is the line. It is in my tables, and it is not my purse.

speaker: edith_kettlewood
text: Now I see it. Now I will laugh, and the laugh is for the line, not for Master Kemp.

speaker: will_kemp
text: I will take a late laugh. I will not take it as payment, and neither will you, which is why I like you.

speaker: john_heminges
text: No one is paying it tonight. Lady Day is the promise, and a promise written is still a promise. I have not got the coin in the parlour.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Then it stands written, and it stands unpaid. Garnish's roll can wait till I am going. The sleeve is the matter.

speaker: edith_kettlewood
text: The sleeve is done. The eight shillings is not done. Do not walk me to the door with another compliment. I have spent the one.

speaker: will_kemp
text: Arms inside the coat, until Lady Day. I shall tell the prince, if I can find which of us he is.

speaker: john_heminges
text: He is the company's prince, and the company will pay when the stock can. Not out of your purse, Will, and not tonight.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Not out of mine. I have written what I was asked to write. Edith, you shall have the day, and you shall not have a speech instead.

speaker: edith_kettlewood
text: The day will do. Eight shillings, Lady Day, and the seam is mine until then, in the sense that I remember it. Good night.

speaker: edith_kettlewood
text: And do not send a boy after me with a finer sentence. The sentence I came for is the one with the sum.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: No boy. No finer sentence. Eight shillings, Lady Day, and the purse stays shut.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Good night. The line will still be there when you want to see it again.
